summary: Adversarial review of the live-arena-fight delta before launch

confirmed.title: Any user can exfiltrate any rival's secret program by issuing one challenge, then reading the envelope feed
confirmed.claim: The envelope feed is "participant-gated," but participation is self-service: the challenge endpoint (line 819) lets any authenticated user create a match where they own the challenger side and name ANY victim's ACTIVE snapshot as defender (only constraint is punch-up gap>=0, satisfiable by building a paperweight in the lowest category). Concrete steps: (1) attacker registers + enlists a minimal robot -> ACTIVE snapshot in the lowest category; (2) picks a rival's ACTIVE snapshot id from the public ladder/scouting card; (3) POST /v1/challenges {challenger=mine, defender=rival} — passes ch.UserId==me and gap>=0, match goes QUEUED; (4) GET /v1/matches/{matchId}/envelopes — the WHERE at line 955 only checks rc.user_id=me OR rd.user_id=me, which the attacker now satisfies, so line 982-983 returns the DEFENDER's full snapshot envelope as human-readable JSON, including the program. Everywhere else in the API the program is guarded (the scouting card at line 570 exposes only program_hash, never the program); this endpoint is the only place a full program leaves the server to a non-owner, and it hands a rival's secret control program to a competitor's account for the price of one ticket + stake, before any fight must actually complete. The design comment (line 939-944) accepts shipping both programs to a participant's DEVICE for local simulation, but the gate treats 'challenged them' as 'entitled to read their IP,' which any user can trivially obtain against any target.
confirmed.why: Verified in server/RobotBrawl.Api/Program.cs. The challenge endpoint (line 819) only checks that the CHALLENGER side is owned by the caller (line 843, ch.UserId != me -> Forbid); the DEFENDER side has no ownership constraint, only a punch-up check (line 856-857, gap = di - ci >= 0). An attacker with a minimal robot in the lowest category (ci=0) satisfies gap>=0 against ANY target, and target active-snapshot ids are publicly discoverable (robots listing line 479, plus the scouting card). Creating the challenge inserts a QUEUED match with the attacker as rc.user_id. The envelope feed (line 945) gate at line 955 is WHERE m.id=$1 AND (rc.user_id=me OR rd.user_id=me) with NO match-status predicate, so the attacker-as-challenger satisfies it immediately, before any fight. Lines 982-983 return both snapshot envelopes as raw UTF-8 JSON, whose payload (line 527) contains the full program. The program is confirmed secret everywhere else: the scouting card (line 570-627) exposes only program_hash and its comment states the payload is worker-only. The ticket/stake cost is a price, not an access control, and the leak happens at QUEUED independent of fight outcome. All refutation attempts (defender ownership, gap blocking, status gating, cost barrier) fail. The defect is real: any authenticated user can exfiltrate any rival's secret program by issuing one challenge and reading the envelope feed.

confirmed.title: Live arena fight pays real single-player profile scrap: Progression.Data is not isolated
confirmed.claim: MatchRunner.Start (lines 222-234) swaps in a scratch CareerData and sets Career.active=false, but never isolates Progression.Data, which is a SEPARATE persisted owner file (robotbrawl_profile.json, Progression.cs:110-111). Sequence: LiveFight -> RunBout -> bm.EnterMatchArena (BuilderManager.cs:5462 sets Progression.rewarded=false, arming settlement for every bout) -> fight ends -> FightManager.End (FightManager.cs:919) -> Progression.OnMatchEnd. With Career.active=false the Career.SettleFight branch (Progression.cs:222) is skipped and the SANDBOX branch runs against the REAL profile: Data.scrap += pay (75 base + up to 100 damage bonus on a win, or up to 100 consolation on a loss - so QUIT-conceding a live ladder match PAYS the player), Data.fightsFought++/fightsWon++, then Save() at Progression.cs:264 writes robotbrawl_profile.json unconditionally (no autosave gate). Every live arena challenge mints free local scrap into the shipped single-player economy - the exact economy the server-side wallet (Server_Economy_Design_2026-08-13) is being built to own - and the results page then displays this lie: FightManager.cs:1216-1218 prints Progression.lastRewardLine ('+94 scrap (exhibition win) - scrap total N') on a LADDER match whose real settlement is the cloud referee's. Bonus leak: MatchRunner saves/restores activeRungIndex but NOT Progression.activeChallengeIdx, which nothing clears at fight END (only at fight STARTS, BuilderManager.cs:4294/4315/4325); if the player fought a P4c challenge earlier in the session and then does a live arena challenge, a live WIN executes Progression.cs:247-257 and permanently completes that challenge (doneChallenges.Add) plus its one-time 200-500 scrap purse, against the wrong opponent with zero constraint validation.
confirmed.why: Confirmed by reading live code. MatchRunner.Start (MatchRunner.cs:222-234) isolates Career.Data/Career.active/activeRungIndex but never Progression.Data, a separate persisted file (robotbrawl_profile.json, Progression.cs:110-111) with a getter-only Data property (no seam to swap a scratch) and an ungated Save() (Progression.cs:134-137). Each live bout calls EnterMatchArena which sets Progression.rewarded=false (BuilderManager.cs:5462), and FightManager.End calls Progression.OnMatchEnd unconditionally (FightManager.cs:919). With Career.active=false the SettleFight branch (Progression.cs:222) is skipped and the exhibition branch pays the REAL profile: win 75 + up to 100 damage bonus, loss 25-100 consolation (so QUIT-conceding at FightManager.cs:976 pays), scrap/fightsFought/fightsWon mutated, then Save() writes the file. It is actually worse than claimed: best-of-3 re-arms rewarded per bout, so one live match settles 2-3 times. The results page confirms the display leg: arenaLive with cIsContest=false draws Progression.lastRewardLine ('+N scrap (exhibition win)') at FightManager.cs:1216-1218 on a ladder match the cloud referee settles. Bonus leak also real: every activeChallengeIdx clear site is a fight-start (BuilderManager.cs 1313/4294/4315/4319/4325/4469/6993, MobileBuilderUI.cs:1431, Phase5Mobile.cs:75), nothing clears it at fight end, and MatchRunner restores only activeRungIndex — a stale idx from a prior LOST/drawn challenge attempt makes a live-arena win execute Progression.cs:247-257 (doneChallenges.Add + one-time 200-500 purse, wrong opponent, no constraint validation). Minor overstatement only: the challenge leak requires the earlier attempt not to have won (a won challenge is already done and pays nothing further); the core defect stands as claimed.

confirmed.title: Every full-length live bout is cut off by the 90s wall-clock cap and mis-scored as a local Draw
confirmed.claim: wallClockCapPerBout = 90 REAL seconds (line 96) was sized for headless speed=10 (90 sim seconds = 9 wall seconds). LiveFight runs MatchRunner at speed 1 (ArenaScreen.cs:437) and never adjusts the cap. The cap clock t0 starts BEFORE the settle phase (MatchRunner.cs:389), and DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME is 90 SIM seconds (FightManager.cs:99), so a bout that goes the distance needs ~1s settle + 90s fight > 90s cap. Sequence: any live fight with no early KO/count-out reaches the cap first, the loop at lines 404-406 exits, and line 408-409 forces fm.End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout") seconds before the real bell - skipping FightManager's judges' decision (structure/damage/control, FightManager.cs:840-878) entirely. The player is told 'a draw - the stake comes back when the referee confirms' (ArenaScreen.cs:450) while the cloud referee, running the identical seed to the actual bell, scores a decision - so the feature's stated premise ('an honest client shows the same ending it later confirms') fails on precisely the fights close enough to go the distance, and the shown fight also ends visibly early with no bell.
confirmed.why: Confirmed in code. MatchRunner.cs:96 sets wallClockCapPerBout=90 REAL seconds (Time.realtimeSinceStartup loops at 391-393 and 404-406), with t0 taken at line 389 BEFORE the 1.2s settle phase (FightManager.SETTLE_TIME=1.2, line 126). ArenaScreen.LiveFight (line 437) runs MatchRunner at speed 1f and sets only liveHold (439); nothing anywhere scales the cap. FightManager's timer is 90 SIM seconds ticked on scaled deltaTime (DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME=90, line 99; Update lines 350-359), so at timeScale 1 a distance bout needs 1.2+90=91.2 real seconds > 90s cap. The cap fires ~1.2s before the bell while state is still Fighting, and lines 408-409 force fm.End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout"), bypassing Judge() (only invoked at timer<=0, line 386). ArenaScreen 444-450 then tells the player it was a draw, while the cloud referee at speed 10 (91.2 sim s ≈ 9 wall s) reaches the real judges' decision on the same seed — diverging on exactly the fights close enough to go the distance. Distance fights are a designed outcome (FightManager comments ~580, ~632: "running the clock down to the judges... is the honest resolution"). Early-end paths (KO, count-out, stall calls, mercy rule) avoid the bug only by ending before the bell; every bout that would reach the bell is mis-scored.

confirmed.title: Exception mid-bout or mid-hold leaves Career.Data permanently swapped to scratch and LiveFight spinning forever
confirmed.claim: The owner-state restore lives in the finally of the OUTER Start() iterator (lines 252-264), but the fight and the liveHold wait run inside the INNER RunBout iterator (line 242's yield return). When an unhandled exception escapes a nested coroutine's MoveNext (any NRE in Setup/SpawnBot/ReplayRecorder/the hold loop), Unity logs it and terminates the coroutine chain WITHOUT resuming or disposing the parent iterator - the outer finally never executes (finally in coroutines runs on StopCoroutine/OnDestroy disposal, not on a child's exception). Resulting state, for the rest of the session: Career.Data = the scratch CareerData (owner career appears wiped in the UI), Career.active=false, Career.autosave=false, builder possibly left in Mode.Fight with the challenger's build loaded over the owner's, dock closed (ArenaScreen.cs:435), and Time.timeScale stuck at `speed`. ArenaScreen.LiveFight waits on `while (!done)` (line 440) forever since onDone only fires from Decide/Fail, so RestoreDock never runs. Escalation to career-file loss: if anything then flips autosave back on - e.g. any concurrent harness's SuspendAutosave holder disposing takes autosaveHolds to 0 and sets autosave=true (Career.cs:628-629) - the next `if (autosave) Save()` career op writes the SCRATCH data over robotbrawl_career.json (baseline md5 18614d0e). Fix shape: onDone/restore must survive an inner-iterator exception (own the hold and restore in one frame-level guard, or move restore into RunBout-level finally + OnDestroy backstop).
confirmed.why: Verified against the code. MatchRunner.cs puts the entire owner-state restore (Career.Data/active/autosave, timeScale, BackToBuild, owner build reload) in the finally of the outer Start() iterator (lines 252-264), while the fight and liveHold wait run in the inner RunBout iterator (yielded at line 242), which has no try/finally and no OnDestroy backstop. An unhandled exception in RunBout is thrown from the inner iterator's MoveNext, which Unity's scheduler logs and drops without resuming or disposing the parent — a C# iterator's finally runs only via its own MoveNext or Dispose(), and nothing disposes the match_runner object in-session — so the outer finally never executes: Career.Data stays the scratch CareerData, autosave/active stay false, the builder stays in arena mode with the challenger's build. onDone fires only from Start()'s post-finally tail or Fail(), so ArenaScreen.LiveFight (dock closed at :435) spins forever on `while (!done)` at :440 and RestoreDock never runs. The escalation is also real: MatchRunner sets Career.autosave=false directly (line 230), bypassing the counted hold, so autosaveHolds is 0; any of the many SuspendAutosave() callers (CareerSmoke, HazardBench, ArenaShots, etc.) disposing takes holds 1→0 and re-arms autosave=true (Career.cs:628-629) while Data is still scratch, and the next `if (autosave) Save()` (Career.cs:507/543/678/690/1028) writes the scratch data over robotbrawl_career.json. Only quibble: in the live path speed=1f, so the stuck-timeScale symptom is real only for bench-speed callers.

confirmed.title: MatchRunner bypasses the counted SuspendAutosave hold with a raw autosave save/restore
confirmed.claim: Lines 223/230/257 capture and restore Career.autosave as a plain bool instead of using Career.SuspendAutosave(), the counted hold built after the 2026-08-10 career-overwrite incident whose comment (Career.cs:589-605) says verbatim that a plain save-and-restore is not safe when two holders overlap. Concrete interleavings, now on a PRODUCT path a player triggers: (a) bench holds SuspendAutosave (holds=1, autosave=false) -> live fight starts, savedAuto=false -> bench disposes mid-fight -> holds=0 sets autosave=TRUE while Career.Data is the scratch -> any `if (autosave) Save()` path writes scratch over robotbrawl_career.json; (b) live fight starts with savedAuto=true -> bench takes a hold mid-fight -> live fight's finally restores autosave=true, silently cancelling the bench's still-active hold. Either direction defeats the counting that closed the original incident.
confirmed.why: Confirmed. MatchRunner.cs:223/230/257 capture and restore Career.autosave as a plain bool and never touch autosaveHolds, while Career.cs:589-608's comment on the counted hold states verbatim that a plain save-and-restore is not safe when holders overlap (the 2026-08-10 career-overwrite incident). Both claimed interleavings check out: (b) a bench holding SuspendAutosave (holds=1) is silently cancelled when the live fight's finally writes autosave=savedAuto(true), after which the bench's test purchases hit the many `if (Career.autosave) Career.Save()` sites (BuilderManager x9, ProgramCanvas x3, TryBuy/TrySell, EconomySync); (a) if a pre-existing hold is disposed mid-fight, holds hits 0 and re-arms autosave=true while Career.Data is MatchRunner's scratch CareerData (line 228), and EconomySync.cs:104 (`if (Career.autosave) Career.Save()`, a background sync independent of fight state) can then write the scratch over robotbrawl_career.json. ArenaScreen.cs:436-437 confirms MatchRunner now runs on the player-triggered live-challenge path. One refutation attempt partially succeeded but does not save the code: Progression.OnMatchEnd's non-career branch calls Progression.Save(), which writes the separate profile file, not the career file — so the per-bout path is not itself a career writer; EconomySync and the hold-cancellation direction (b) keep the defect real. Same raw pattern also exists in ValidateWorkerLoop.cs, WorkerHost.cs, MedalDev.cs and CareerShot.cs — the defect is wider than the claim, not narrower.

confirmed.title: Live fight wall cap (90s) is shorter than settle + full match at speed 1 — every distance fight ends as 'match wall timeout' draw
confirmed.claim: LiveFight runs MatchRunner at speed=1f with the default wallClockCapPerBout=90f, but t0 is taken BEFORE the 1.2s settle window and DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME is 90s of sim time from the bell — so a fight that goes the distance needs 91.2s of wall clock and the cap fires at 90.0s (88.8s of fight time): RunBout's loop exits, calls fm.End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout"), and the player sees a DRAW results page plus 'a draw — the stake comes back when the referee confirms' while the cloud referee (speed 10, same 90s cap = 900 sim-seconds of headroom) reaches the real timer verdict, which can be a loss that takes the stake. With the 43% mutual-disarm rate many ladder fights run to the clock, so this is the common case, not a corner. Worse on a device: Time.realtimeSinceStartup advances across an iOS suspend, so backgrounding the app for >90s mid-fight (a phone call, the hunt's backgrounding case) force-ends the fight as a timeout draw the frame the player returns, and any pause or frame hitch also eats the budget. The cap was tuned for 10x benches; a live speed-1 fight needs cap >= settle + match time + slack (or a cap measured in sim time).
confirmed.why: Verified in code: ArenaScreen.LiveFight (ArenaScreen.cs:437) runs MatchRunner at speed=1f without overriding wallClockCapPerBout=90f (MatchRunner.cs:96). t0 is taken at MatchRunner.cs:389 BEFORE the settle loop, and both loops (391-393, 404-406) measure Time.realtimeSinceStartup against that t0. FightManager has SETTLE_TIME=1.2f and DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME=90f, decremented with scaled deltaTime (1:1 with wall clock at timeScale=1, slower under frame hitches since deltaTime is clamped by maximumDeltaTime while realtime is not). A fight that runs the timer down needs ~91.2s of wall clock, so the 90.0s cap fires first (timer still ~1.2s), the loop exits with fm.state != Ended, and MatchRunner.cs:408-409 calls fm.End(Draw, "match wall timeout") — the judges' verdict (which can be a stake-taking loss) never runs on the client, and ArenaScreen.cs:450 tells the player "a draw — the stake comes back when the referee confirms" while the authoritative cloud referee (speed 10 = ~900 sim-seconds of headroom under the same 90s wall cap) can settle it as a loss. Time.realtimeSinceStartup also advances across an iOS suspend, so backgrounding >90s mid-fight force-ends it as a timeout draw on resume. One nuance: the claim's frequency argument overstates — mutually-disarmed fights usually end early via STALL_QUIET=12s stalemate→judges, not at the clock — but every genuine distance fight (timeout→judges is a designed outcome per FightManager.cs:14) deterministically hits this cap, so the defect is real.

confirmed.title: Confirming a challenge while a replay plays starts the live fight in the replay's arena — two owners of BuildArena, BackToBuild lands mid-fight
confirmed.claim: Device sequence: MY FIGHTS -> WATCH (dock closes, replay plays, tab strip stays visible because ReplayPlayer creates no FightManager so the canvas stays enabled) -> tap the ARENA tab button (MobileBuilderUI.cs:532 reopens the dock; ShowTab keeps the replay because i==4) -> board -> scout -> challenge -> CONFIRM. ConfirmChallenge/DoChallenge/LiveFight check only `busy`, never `Playing` (`player != null`), unlike Watch() which closes any prior player first. LiveFight then runs MatchRunner.RunBout, whose bm.BackToBuild() (MatchRunner.cs:314) destroys the replay's arena and bots while ReplayPlayer keeps running against them; when the recording ends its callback fires StopReplay() -> player.Close() -> bm.BackToBuild() (ReplayPlayer.cs:253) in the MIDDLE of the live fight, tearing the arena down under FightManager/MatchRunner (BuildArena is documented non-idempotent), then RestoreDock() reopens the dock over the wrecked fight. The stake was already charged by the POST. LiveFight/DoChallenge must StopReplay() before starting the runner.
confirmed.why: Confirmed in code. ShowTab (MobileBuilderUI.cs:4421) stops a replay only when leaving tab 4, and the ARENA tab button (:532) reopens the dock without stopping it — a deliberately supported state (the STOP REPLAY button at :3082 exists for it). ConfirmChallenge (ArenaScreen.cs:775) gates only on busy/card; Scout/ArmChallenge/DoChallenge/LiveFight never check Playing (player != null) and never StopReplay — only Watch closes a prior player (:206). LiveFight starts MatchRunner.Run whose RunBout calls bm.BackToBuild() (MatchRunner.cs:314), destroying the replay's bots/arena under the still-running ReplayPlayer, and even reuses the replay's FightCamera on Camera.main (:345). ReplayPlayer.Update keeps advancing time and at duration fires the Watch callback (ArenaScreen.cs:252): StopReplay -> Close -> Destroy(cam) + bm.BackToBuild() (ReplayPlayer.cs:250-254) mid-live-fight — tearing down the live arena while MatchRunner spins on fm.state (:404) — then RestoreDock reopens the dock over the wreck. The stake was charged by the Challenge POST before LiveFight (:401). Only mitigations: a replay that ends before the runner starts is harmless, and the cloud referee still settles the match; neither refutes the reachable interleaving. Fix as claimed: StopReplay() before starting the runner.

confirmed.title: Envelope-fetch failure downgrade is invisible: message written to SC_INBOX while the player is on the board, and showInbox is never set
confirmed.claim: In LiveFight (line 431), when MatchEnvelopes fails (offline blip, 404) the downgrade message 'the fight runs in the cloud — <err>' is Say()'d with scope SC_INBOX, but showInbox is left false and DoChallenge's success callback has already cleared `card` — so the dock is showing the BOARD surface, where the §2.4 scope rule suppresses both this message and DoChallenge's 'challenge accepted — N scrap staked' (SC_CARD, card now null). Concrete player experience: tap CONFIRM, stake is charged server-side, and the screen shows only 'N ranked' with no acknowledgement that anything happened; the fight silently appears in MY FIGHTS later. The success path sets showInbox=true before speaking; the failure path needs the same (set showInbox=true before the Say, mirroring line 443).
confirmed.why: Confirmed in code. ArenaScreen.cs:430-431 speaks the envelope-failure downgrade with scope SC_INBOX and yields break without setting showInbox; DoChallenge's success callback (line 408) has already nulled `card`, so MobileBuilderUI.RefreshArena (lines 3373-3376) selects the BOARD surface, whose renderer (lines 3447-3458) shows ArenaScreen.Status only when StatusScope == SC_BOARD and otherwise prints "CATEGORY · N ranked" — suppressing both the SC_INBOX downgrade and the orphaned SC_CARD "challenge accepted — N scrap staked" (lines 406-407). The success path (line 443) sets showInbox = true before its SC_INBOX Say, proving the intended pattern the failure path omits. The stake is genuinely debited server-side at challenge creation in one transaction (Program.cs:908-924), so the player is charged and sees no acknowledgement. Fix matches the claim: set showInbox = true (and showEnlist = false) before the Say at line 431.

confirmed.title: Live bout at speed 1 cannot finish inside the 90s WALL cap - full-distance fights end 'match wall timeout' Draw on device while the worker judges a winner
confirmed.claim: wallClockCapPerBout = 90f WALL seconds (line 96), and t0 = Time.realtimeSinceStartup is set BEFORE the settle wait (line 389). At the worker's speed 10 (FightWorkerLoop.SpeedMultiplier = 10f), SETTLE_TIME 1.2s + DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME 90s of sim fits in ~9-10 wall seconds and the judges rule on damage. In the live client (ArenaScreen.LiveFight passes speed 1f), the same bout needs 1.2 + 90 = 91.2+ wall seconds, so the wait loop at lines 404-409 exits at 90 and calls fm.End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout") ~1.2 sim-seconds before Judge() would fire. Every challenge that goes the distance shows the player a Draw ending that the cloud referee will settle as a win or loss - deterministically, by arithmetic, with zero physics divergence needed. iOS makes it worse: frame hitches and app suspension (realtimeSinceStartup keeps advancing across an iOS suspend) burn the same budget, so even shorter fights can be cut.
confirmed.why: Confirmed by direct code reading. MatchRunner.cs:96 sets wallClockCapPerBout=90f (wall seconds) and nothing in the live path overrides it; ArenaScreen.cs:437-439 runs the live match at speed 1f with liveHold=true only. MatchRunner.cs:389 captures t0 = Time.realtimeSinceStartup BEFORE the settle-wait loop, and both loops (392, 405) gate on the same t0 vs the 90s cap. FightManager.cs:350-359 decrements settleLeft (SETTLE_TIME=1.2) and timer (DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME=90) by scaled Time.deltaTime, so at timeScale=1 a full-distance bout needs >=91.2 wall seconds before Judge() fires at timer<=0 (line 386) — sim time can only lag wall time (maximumDeltaTime clamps hitches), never lead it. The loop at 404-406 therefore exits at 90 wall (~88.8 sim into the fight) and lines 408-409 call fm.End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout") ~1.2 sim-seconds before the judges would rule. FightWorkerLoop.cs:41,93 runs the identical bout at SpeedMultiplier=10f (~9.1 wall sec), reaches Judge(), and settles on damage — so every challenge that goes the distance shows the player a Draw the server settles as a win/loss. Deterministic arithmetic (90 < 1.2 + 90); no physics divergence required. arenaLive only affects QUIT-concede (FightManager.cs:976) and the results page, not the timer or cap. Fights ending early (KO/count-out/stalemate) are unaffected, but the timeout-to-judges outcome class is unreachable on device.

confirmed.title: The premise itself: PhysX on iOS arm64 and Linux x64 is not cross-platform deterministic, and the results copy promises the purse before the referee rules
confirmed.claim: The design assumes 'same server seed = same fight' between an iOS device build and the Linux worker player. Unity's PhysX integration is not deterministic across architectures/compilers (different FMA contraction, float accumulation order, solver SIMD paths), and a robot-combat sim is chaotic - one ULP at first contact diverges into a different winner. The seed only fixes the SPAWN (MatchRunner.SpawnPoses draws 3 values); everything after is unseeded physics. ArenaScreen.LiveFight (line ~449) then prints "VICTORY — the referee is confirming; the purse is on its way" off the LOCAL result - an assertion, not a hedge - so any divergence becomes a player-visible lie when settlement pays the other way. Either the copy must present the local fight as a preview, or the client must reconcile against the referee's verdict when it lands.
confirmed.why: Every factual leg checks out in the code, and the project's own design doc refutes the feature's premise. (1) The seed fixes only the spawn: MatchRunner.SpawnPoses (line ~193) calls UnityEngine.Random.InitState(seed) and draws 3 values; MatchRunner's header explicitly says stepped Physics.Simulate was NOT used — the fight rides the automatic FixedUpdate PhysX loop, unseeded (FightManager even draws unseeded Random mid-fight at :237). (2) Multiplayer_V3_Design_Doc.md §5.4 states in so many words: "Cross-machine physics determinism is NOT assumed... Same-binary, same-machine runs are repeatable enough for debugging; that is all we need" — yet today's change (server Program.cs:874-880) retired best-of-3 down to ONE server seed and asserts the same seed "makes the on-device fight and the settlement fight one fight" (iOS arm64 device vs Linux x64 worker — exactly the cross-machine case §5.4 disavows), with no measurement anywhere in docs/. Single-bout also removes the best-of-3 damping §5.4 relied on, so any divergence flips the whole match. (3) ArenaScreen.cs:446-450 prints "VICTORY — the referee is confirming; the purse is on its way" (and equally assertive defeat/draw lines) off the LOCAL MatchRunner result — an outcome promise, not a preview. (4) No reconciliation: Refresh() (lines 156-160) uses newly-settled inbox entries only to kick EconomySync for the wallet; nothing compares the locally shown verdict to the referee's settled outcome or corrects the player on divergence. Mitigants ("the referee is confirming" is a partial hedge; the inbox eventually shows the true outcome) don't cure the unconditional purse promise, and the project's own data (43% mutual disarm, ±17-point wander at N=12) establishes the sim as chaotic enough for ULP-level divergence to change winners.

confirmed.title: The entire referee runs in Update() on scaled Time.deltaTime - every end condition is quantized to RENDER frames, which differ ~10-20x in sim-time granularity between client and worker
confirmed.claim: FightManager.Update (line 347-388) ticks settleLeft, elapsed, timer, TickShove, TickCountOut (flipped/immobile accumulation), TickStalemate and the timeout Judge with dt = Time.deltaTime, and samples robot state once per rendered frame. On device at speed 1 / 60fps the referee polls every ~0.017 sim-s; on the headless worker at speed 10 a frame covers ~0.17-0.33 sim-s (Time.maximumDeltaTime clamps at 1/3 s, i.e. up to ~20 physics steps between polls). Consequences: the Bell() fires at a frame boundary so controls unfreeze at a different offset into the fixed-step sequence (the fight is phase-shifted from t=0 even with identical seeds); count-out timers sample flipped/immobile state at 10-20x coarser cadence on the worker, so a bot flickering across the threshold accumulates differently; KO/count-out/stalemate/timeout all land on different sim times. Any end condition that is close on one side can resolve differently on the other. The referee clock and state sampling belong in FixedUpdate on fixedDeltaTime.
confirmed.why: Confirmed in code. FightManager.Update (Assets/Phase1/Scripts/FightManager.cs:347-388) ticks every referee clock and end condition with dt = Time.deltaTime (line 350) and samples robot state once per rendered frame (Poll, 361-362); there is no FixedUpdate referee. Speed is implemented as Time.timeScale (MatchRunner.cs:390), the client live fight runs at 1f (ArenaScreen.cs:437) while the worker runs the identical referee at SpeedMultiplier=10f (FightWorkerLoop.cs:41,93), so the worker's referee polls ~10x coarser in sim time (up to the Time.maximumDeltaTime clamp of 1/3 s; no project override or captureDeltaTime mitigation exists). TickCountOut (line 508) credits a whole frame's dt to a single per-frame sample of the flipped/velocity thresholds (513, 519), so threshold-flickering bots accumulate flippedTime/immobileTime/incapTimer differently on the two sides, and those totals also feed the judges (804, 818-819). Bell() fires at a frame boundary (353-354), phase-shifting control unfreeze relative to the fixed-step sequence. Net effect: any end condition that is close on one side (count-out, stalemate call, timeout-vs-KO) can resolve at a different sim time or a different outcome on the other despite identical seeds, so the on-device fight can contradict the cloud settlement — exactly the defect claimed. Only caveat: the precise 10-20x factor depends on the worker's actual frame cadence, but the structural mechanism is exactly as described and the claimed range is consistent with targetFrameRate=60 (Phase0Bootstrap.cs:28) and the maximumDeltaTime clamp.

confirmed.title: The seeded Random stream is shared with wall-clock-rate-limited cosmetics - shard debris (real physics bodies) get different velocities on client vs worker
confirmed.claim: MatchRunner.SpawnPoses calls UnityEngine.Random.InitState(seed) on the GLOBAL stream, and CompoundRobot.SpawnShards (lines 1195-1217) later draws ~13 values per destroyed part to set positions, rotations and VELOCITIES of Rigidbody shards that live 6s with live colliders and can strike the robots. Between those two points the same global stream is consumed by: FightManager.Setup's music pick (line 237, 1 draw); SfxSynth.Clang via the RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod OnHit hook (SfxSynth.cs 165-172) - 2 draws per hit but rate-limited on Time.unscaledTime (0.07 WALL s), so at speed 10 the worker skips ~10x more clangs per sim-second than the client does at speed 1, i.e. the draw COUNTS differ by design; FloatingDamageSpawner (attached to the arena root in BuildArena, so present headless too) whose per-hit draws depend on a frame-rate-dependent 0.45s merge window; CrowdAudio.Begin at the bell, whose one-time clip synthesis burns thousands of draws on the FIRST fight of a session only (client's first live fight vs the worker's Nth queued job). Net: by the first part destruction the two environments are at different stream positions, shard impulses differ, and shard-robot collisions convert cosmetic randomness into trajectory divergence. Fight-affecting randomness needs its own System.Random seeded from the match seed, never UnityEngine.Random.
confirmed.why: Confirmed in code. MatchRunner.cs:193 seeds the GLOBAL UnityEngine.Random stream; CompoundRobot.SpawnShards (1196-1218) later draws ~39 global-stream values per destroyed part (3 shards x position/rotation/velocity/angularVelocity) for Rigidbody cubes with live default-layer colliders that persist 6s and can strike robots. Between seed and shard spawn the same stream is consumed by: FightManager.Setup music pick (line 237); SfxSynth.Clang (2 draws/hit, auto-subscribed to DamageResolver.OnHit via RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod so it runs headless, rate-limited on Time.unscaledTime 0.07 WALL s — and the worker runs timeScale 10 (FightWorkerLoop.SpeedMultiplier=10f) vs the client live fight's 1f (ArenaScreen:437), so draw counts per sim-second differ by construction); FloatingDamageSpawner (attached to arena root at BuilderManager:3985, draws gated by 0.45s/1.5s timing windows); and CrowdAudio.Begin at the bell (FightManager:302) whose first-call Ensure() synthesis burns hundreds of draws only on the first fight of a process. No reseeding and no shard collision isolation exists. Net: client and worker reach part destruction at different stream positions, shard impulses differ, and shard-robot collisions convert cosmetic randomness into fight divergence vs settlement. Only nit: '~13 values' is per shard, not per part (~39 per part) — immaterial to the mechanism.

confirmed.title: AIController phases off ABSOLUTE session time: flip-wiggle Sin(Time.time*6f), decision-tick anchor, and the opening-caution clock all differ between a device session and a worker job
confirmed.claim: The flipped branch drives throttle/steer from Mathf.Sin(Time.time * 6f) and Sin(Time.time * 3f) (~line 300) - Time.time is seconds since SESSION start, so the wiggle phase at the moment a bot flips depends on how long the player sat in menus (device) vs how many jobs the worker has drained (Linux), and the two sims wiggle in different directions. Same class: nextDecision = Time.time + rtDecision (FixedUpdate, line 217-222) anchors the 5 Hz decision grid to when the component was enabled, and OnEnable captures activeSince = Time.time during FightManager.Bell() - an Update-frame timestamp - so the 3s OPENING_TIME reduced-throttle window and every subsequent decision boundary sit at different offsets relative to the physics steps on the two sides. All of these should be anchored to bell time measured in fixed time (or driven from a per-fight tick counter), not absolute Time.time.
confirmed.why: Verified in Assets/Phase1/Scripts/AIController.cs. (1) Flipped branch, lines 310-311: throttle/steer are the sign of Mathf.Sin(Time.time*6f)/Sin(Time.time*3f) — absolute session-time phase, so wiggle direction at flip time depends on device menu-idle vs how many jobs the worker (which drains the whole queue per invocation) has already run. (2) Lines 217-222: nextDecision = Time.time + rtDecision in FixedUpdate anchors the 5 Hz decision grid to component enable in absolute session time. (3) Lines 210-215 + 570: OnEnable captures activeSince = Time.time, and FightManager.Bell() runs from Update() (FightManager.cs:347-354), so the anchor is a variable-frame timestamp compared later against fixedTime in FixedUpdate — the 3 s OPENING_TIME window spans a frame-pacing-dependent number of physics steps, and pacing differs device vs headless Linux worker. Refutations failed: AIController IS in the ladder path — MatchRunner.cs:364-379 attaches it whenever a snapshot has program=="", which RobotSnapshot.cs:46-47 documents as a legitimate AI-driven snapshot; and single-seed challenges exist precisely so the device fight replays the settlement fight, which absolute-time phase breaks. Caveat: cross-platform PhysX nondeterminism is an additional divergence source, so fixing these clocks is necessary but possibly not sufficient for identical sims; the claim about what the code does is accurate.

confirmed.title: Live fight wall-clock cap ends every full-length challenge before the bell, as a Draw the referee won't settle
confirmed.claim: MatchRunner.wallClockCapPerBout is 90 REAL seconds (line 96) and the bout loop (lines 391-409) counts settle + fight against it. LiveFight runs at speed 1x (ArenaScreen.cs:437 passes 1f), so a challenge that goes the distance needs SETTLE_TIME 1.2s + DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME 90s = ~91.2 real seconds — the cap fires ~1.2 sim-seconds BEFORE FightManager.Judge(), forcing fm.End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout") (line 409). The cloud referee runs the same seed at SpeedMultiplier 10 (~9 real s/bout), reaches the bell, and scores a judges' decision. Every live challenge decided at the final bell — exactly the close fights — shows the player a timeout DRAW and "a draw — the stake comes back" while settlement may take the stake. Fix: scale the cap by speed or set liveHold cap to >= (SETTLE_TIME + DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME)/speed + margin.
confirmed.why: Confirmed in code. MatchRunner.wallClockCapPerBout = 90f real seconds (MatchRunner.cs:96, never overridden — only 3 refs in codebase), and t0 is taken before the settle loop, so settle + fight share the 90 s real budget (lines 390-406), with line 408-409 forcing End(Outcome.Draw, "match wall timeout") on expiry. ArenaScreen.LiveFight runs at speed 1f (ArenaScreen.cs:437) and sets only liveHold, not the cap. FightManager decrements settleLeft (SETTLE_TIME=1.2f) and timer (DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME=90f) with scaled Time.deltaTime, so at timeScale 1 reaching Judge() at the bell needs >= 91.2 real seconds — strictly over the cap, so every bout that would go to a judges' decision is instead force-ended as a timeout Draw ~1.2 sim-seconds before the bell (frame hitches, capped by maximumDeltaTime, only widen the gap). The cloud referee runs the same seeds at the default speed 10 (~9.1 real s/bout), reaches Judge(), and can settle a win/loss while the client told the player "a draw — the stake comes back when the referee confirms" (ArenaScreen.cs:452). No unscaled-time path, no live cap override, and no early-end path rescues bell-decided fights. The proposed fix (scale cap by speed / size liveHold cap to (SETTLE_TIME+DEFAULT_MATCH_TIME)/speed + margin) is correct.

confirmed.title: LiveFight verdict message keys on win counts, not res.verdict — damage-band decisions reported as draws
confirmed.claim: ArenaScreen.LiveFight (lines 444-450) picks its money message from res.aWins/res.bWins. With one seed, a bout that ends Outcome.Draw with unequal damage — Double KO (FightManager.cs:365), double count-out (:378), or the wall-timeout above — leaves aWins==bWins==0, so the client says "a draw — the stake comes back", while MatchRunner.Decide() (MatchRunner.cs:288-292) resolves the SAME result to verdict "A"/"B" by the damage band, and the worker posts CHALLENGER/DEFENDER via ToApiVerdict — the stake settles as a win/loss. The client already holds the correct field: use res.verdict ("A"/"B"/"Draw"), the same one the referee maps.
confirmed.why: Confirmed. ArenaScreen.LiveFight (ArenaScreen.cs:444-450) picks the verdict message from res.aWins/res.bWins and never reads res.verdict, which MatchRunner.MatchResult exposes (MatchRunner.cs:75). Challenges are single-seed (server Program.cs:880), and a bout ending Outcome.Draw — Double KO (FightManager.cs:365), double count-out (:378), or wall timeout (MatchRunner.cs:409) — maps to bout.winner="Draw" (MatchRunner.cs:424-425) with aDealt/bDealt still recorded, leaving aWins==bWins==0. MatchRunner.Decide() (:286-294) then resolves the tie by the FightManager.DrawBand damage margin to verdict "A"/"B" (decidedBy="damage"), and the worker posts ToApiVerdict(result.verdict) → CHALLENGER/DEFENDER (FightWorkerLoop.cs:149), so the stake settles as a win/loss while the client told the player "a draw — the stake comes back". The Draw-with-unequal-damage state is reachable: the Double KO/double count-out/timeout paths bypass FightManager's own band check at :836, and nothing equalizes dealt damage on those outcomes. Fix as claimed: key the message on res.verdict, the same field the referee maps.
